business_thesis: Borana manufactures unbleached synthetic grey fabric and polyester textured yarn, serving fashion, traditional textiles, technical textiles, and home décor segments. The company operates a capital-light, high-ROCE manufacturing model with potential for 3-4 new looming units annually and export expansion into specialty segments.
bull_case: Consistent ROE > 30% and ROCE > 30% for 3+ years demonstrates capital efficiency; recent 35-36% quarterly profitability shows scaling
Rapid capacity expansion: 4x looming units since FY22 (single unit → 4 units), 9.9MW hybrid power plant coming Oct-Dec 2026; capability to add 1 unit/year
Export growth from 10% → 25%+ of revenue; grey fabric is 90%+ of revenue (high-margin specialty); demand tailwinds from India's textile export push
Fresh IPO (late 2024) with strong take-up; public market validation; management track record (promoters have 65% holding; reinvesting profits)
bear_case: Working capital intensity has increased from 16 days (FY24) to 87 days (FY26), raising cash requirements for growth capex; cash conversion cycle deteriorating
Dependency on grey fabric (~90% revenue) creates concentration risk; limited diversification into finished goods or value-added segments
Debt increased from ₹61Cr (FY25) to ₹71Cr (FY26) to fund 9.9MW capex; hybrid power plant cost delays risk (revised to Oct-Dec 2026)
Smaller scale vs. peers (KPR Mills ₹36.6K Cr, Welspun ₹21.7K Cr); pricing power limited against larger competitors; commodity yarn cost exposure
thesis_rationale: High ROCE + disciplined capex + export tailwinds suggest potential for 20-25% CAGR over next 3 years; at 10.5x P/E with 35% ROE, room for 2.5-3x return if ROCE maintained and capacity scales 3-4 units.
key_catalysts: 9.9MW hybrid power plant commissioning (Oct-Dec 2026) → lower energy costs, EBITDA margin expansion to 26-27%
Q2/Q3 FY27 capacity utilization ramp (new looming units) → gross margin improvement from supply-demand tightness in export markets
Potential entry into value-added textiles (dyed/printed fabric) or technical textiles segment → higher ASP/ROCE
Data center demand spillover (potential: electrical/thermal efficiency benefits of specialty fabrics) → new TAM exploration
key_risks: Rapid debt accumulation if capex overshoots; hybrid power plant delays could dent FY27 margins
Export demand slowdown (US/EU recession) could reduce grey fabric ASP and volume
Competition from larger mills on pricing; working capital stretch if receivables days extend further
Operational execution risk on new looming units (supply chain, training, utilization ramp)
verdict_rationale: Attractive entry at 10.5x P/E given 35% ROE and 32.5% ROCE; capital-efficient, capacity-expansion story with export tailwinds and energy cost benefits post-hybrid plant. Risk of WC intensity and competition manageable vs. upside if ROCE sustains and units scale.
key_metrics_to_track: New looming unit utilization ramp (target: >80% by Q4 FY27)
Hybrid power plant EBITDA benefit (estimate: 150-200 bps margin uplift)
